est écrite comme elle se règle dans un c: is written the way it is set in a pitch corrector or a DAW: the note (Key) then the scale (Scale). For “A minor”, choose Key: A and Scale: Minor. A black key has two names depending on the software (F# or Gb): both are shown. If the track is not tuned to A = 440 Hz, the deviation is shown in cents under “Detune”: that is the value to enter in the setting of the same name, otherwise the correction sounds out of tune. Below come the French name (La mineur) and the Camelot code (8A, used by DJs to blend two tracks). A major key and its relative minor share the same notes: C major and A minor, for example. If your ear tells you the other one, the second suggestion is probably right.
est le nombre de temps par minute. Un mê: is the number of beats per minute. The same track can be counted twice as fast or twice as slow: 70 and 140 BPM describe the same pulse, felt on the quarter or the eighth note. The tool shows the most likely reading and the other one below.
